comments.body:
It seems like some LLM has triaged this and made a comment that seems like half a suggestion and half a misunderstanding. `atomicBinOp` *does not have* a parameter for the sample index, so it does not "belong" anywhere and yes it would pass validation because an undefined third texture coordinate for a `RWTexture2D` is perfectly normal (it would have to reject it based on `RWTexture2DMS` not being supported rather than not putting the sample index "where it belongs"). *In theory*, the third texture coordinate parameter could be used as the sample index for `RWTexture2DMS`, but then where does it go for `RWTexture2DMSArray`, which already needs the third coordinate? We would need to do some bitpacking shenanigans and in either case driver compilers need to be updated to interpret all of this correctly. It is currently unclear what driver compilers actually do here and whether they even technically pull from the undef coordinate in the non-array case at all. I also don't know which hardware actually supports those atomics, it might be a different set than what currently reports SM6.7+.

All of this feels like new shader model territory rather than a "quick fix", at which point there should be a completely new DXIL instruction with an extra sample index parameter if you want to go that path instead of just rejecting the code. This is what happened with `textureStore`; a new `textureStoreSample` variant was added with an extra sample index parameter instead of forcefully shoehorning it into an existing parameter that is already used for something else, because that would just mean more silent UB or misunderstandings.

I also find it hilarious that this is listed by the bot in the list of issues it "cannot reproduce" even though it clearly can.

@Maraneshi - sorry for the noise.  I'm experimenting with some auto-triaging tooling and although it's all meant to be done in my fork and not post anything, it tagged the issue in a commit message which is what showed up for you here.  Thank you for the explanation and catching this.

Yeah, I see now that it does have a longer explanation too that does correctly state that the atomic should be immediately rejected based on the resource type. Just the sentence about the sample index was weird/wrong and indicated not understanding what's going on. If you feel there is a better title for this issue you can of course change it.

title: Atomics on RWTexture2DMS result in silent UB or ICE
